body_text:
The *characteristic* $\operatorname{char}(R)$ of a ring with
identity is the least positive integer $n$ such that
$n \cdot 1 = 0$, if such an integer exists, and is $0$
otherwise.

Equivalently, the characteristic is the unique non-negative
generator of the kernel of the canonical ring homomorphism
$\chi : \mathbb{Z} \to R$ defined by $\chi(m) = m \cdot 1$.

In an integral domain $D$, if $n \cdot 1 = 0$ with
$n = a \cdot b$, then $(a \cdot 1) \cdot (b \cdot 1) = 0$
forces $a \cdot 1 = 0$ or $b \cdot 1 = 0$. Hence the
characteristic of an integral domain (and therefore of any
field) is either $0$ or a prime number $p$. Consequently, every
field contains a unique minimal prime subfield: either the
rational field $\mathbb{Q}$ (if $\operatorname{char}(F) = 0$)
or the finite Galois field
$\mathbb{F}_p = \mathbb{Z}/p\mathbb{Z}$ (if
$\operatorname{char}(F) = p$).
